source_title: Delhi Police grants Congress rally at Ramlila Maidan with strict conditions, denies mock impeachment request - The Hindu
source_excerpt: NEW DELHI The Delhi Police on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) said they had not received any request seeking permission for a proposed mock “public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on October 30 and November 1, denying reports that permission for the proposed events had been refused. The police, however, confirmed that they have given a no-objection to the INDIA bloc’s November 1 rally against the irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, reiterating its demand for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation. Also Read: Delhi Police grants Congress NOC for November 1 rally at Ramlila Maidan https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/delhi-police-allows-congress-to-hold-rally-at-ramlila-maidan-on-november-1/article71596438.ece Speaking to The Hindu, Deputy Commissioner of Police (Central) Rohit Rajbir Singh said the Congress had sought permission only for a rally by the INDIA bloc at Ramlila Maidan on November 1, which was granted subject to several conditions. No separate request for a mock impeachment had been received, he said. Delhi traders flag potential impact on 21 markets from November 1 Congress rally, seek postponement Delhi traders flag potential impact on 21 markets from November 1 Congress rally, seek postponement It projected that the November 1 rally could bring commercial activity across Old Delhi to a standstill, resulting in losses of up to ₹10,000 crore Delhi traders flag potential impact on 21 markets from INDIA bloc’s November 1 rally, seek postponement storyline 1 As per the permission letter issued by the Central district police, as reported by The Hindu, the rally is scheduled to be held from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. on November 1. The no-objection from the law and order perspective is subject to the organisers obtaining prior permission from the land-owning authority. Also Read: Congress rally on November 1: What are the conditions imposed by Delhi Police https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Delhi/congress-rally-november-1-ramlila-maidan-restrictions-by-delhi-police/article71635407.ece The conditions for the November 1 rally include installing high-definition CCTV cameras at strategic points across the venue, including entry and exit gates, the stage and seating enclosures, along with a control room and five screens as part of the monitoring system. Organisers have also been asked to provide adequate water tankers and toilet facilities, including separate toilets for women, and deploy sufficient volunteers to manage the gathering. The police have directed the organisers to ensure that the rally remains peaceful and concludes by 5 p.m., with dispersal beginning thereafter. Overnight stays at the venue before or after the rally will not be permitted, and vehicles must be parked at locations designated by the Traffic Unit. ‘Desist from targeting Hindu festivals, economy’: VHP to Opposition over November 1 rally ‘Desist from targeting Hindu festivals, economy’: VHP to Opposition over November 1 rally The remarks came a day after traders held a protest at Kashmere Gate in New Delhi, demanding that Congress defer the November 1 rally until after Diwali. ‘Desist from targeting Hindu festivals, economy’: VHP to Opposition over November 1 rally storyline 1 The permission letter also states that no march will be allowed towards any location outside Ramlila Maidan. Organisers have been asked to submit the list of invitees and volunteers, a minute-by-minute programme, and details of buses, including their registration numbers. The police have further directed the organisers to ensure that no speeches disturb public harmony or contain inflammatory or intimidating content. If any such speech is made, the public address system must be switched off immediately and the speaker removed from the stage. The letter warns that any breach of the conditions or failure to comply with police directions could lead to legal action against the organisers and revocation of the permission.
